name: Write the metric definitions register
text_content:
Type: document

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page section 8.5 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

The shared definitions every mechanism uses: customer, known customer, recognition, return, service period, incident, closed loop, employee NPS, cultural labor score, customer recognition rate, cross-period movement, and every operating metric. Each entry carries the definition, its source in the record, the calculation the stack runs, one owner, the counterweight, the mechanism that reads it and its rhythm, the horizon, and the parent commitment. A metric without an entry is not published. Depends on the cultural labor score decision and on the hub confirmation.

comment.text: Session 13 adds two definitions and two vocabulary lines: a day, as a calendar day on which a person worked a scheduled shift of any length in any period, counted once, every paid block counting as shift; the pool, as the day's built-in share of a defined base at a defined proportion, one per calendar day for the whole house; "the review," unqualified, as the person's review with every other review named in full; and "points," unqualified, as the pay system's word appearing on no other surface. S13 page, header and section 9.5; P24.

comment.text: Session 12 files a vocabulary line for the definitions register: "feedback" names three acts in the record (feedback about tools, WP p.17; feedback upward and on the channel, WP pp. 19 and 22; feedback to a person about their work, WP p.18) and the record never distinguishes them; the S12 page uses "feedback" for the act to a person and names the others by their surfaces. The word "disengaged" (WP p.14) is the one predicate the record attaches to a person and is kept off every lead's mouth. S12 page, findings 18.3 and 18.10.
